newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen shaky over 112 before dive to 109.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen shaky over 112 before dive to 109.

text.p: Dollar/yen is catching its breath after a harrowing decline was interrupted overseas, but analysts said 112 should be the platform from which it plunges to major support at 109.

"In the short term, the bounce we've seen from 112 (yen) is likely to fail below 114.10. I'd suggest selling anywhere between 113.80 and 114.20 (yen), for 109," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Two long-term Fibonacci objectives converge around 109 yen, analysts said.

The 38.2-percent retracement of the entire rally from 79.75 in April 1995 to 127.46 yen this month comes in at 109.20. In addition, 108.70 yen marks the 61.8 percent retrace of the steady advance from 97.10 in September 1995, they said.
After consolidating its steep losses last week, the dollar tumbled more than three percent against the yen early Tuesday, before getting a toehold at 111.98.

But analysts cautioned that Tuesday could be more of a fundamental day than a technical session, with the dollar's next move probably hinging on the outcome of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting.
An announcement on interest rates is expected around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
"Some hourly studies are looking pretty constructive, so if the Fed does raise rates there could be an opportunity for a short squeeze," said John Moore, foreign exchange analyst at Technical Data.
But Moore said if they don't raise rates, then the bias is very much to the downside, with good targets being 109 or possibly 105 yen.

"Part of the reason dollar/yen is so weak is it seems like investment banks and hedge funds are revising their interest rate expectations and that is impacting upon once very profitable yen-carry trades," Moore said.
Elsewhere, dollar/mark is expected to catch the dollar's downdraft against the yen after failing to make headway above 1.71 marks on Monday.

"Dollar/mark is about to accelerate lower," Spain said. "The abject failure last night circa 1.71 has seen it return to the bottom of the short-term range at 1.6850. But while capped below 1.7020/40, we look for a break of the range towards the downside."
Below 1.6840 marks, Spain said he looks for a return to last week's low near 1.6690, then to the more important 1.66 mark level, where bottoms from late March, early April lie.
At 1200 EDT on Tuesday, the dollar was trading at 1.6950/55 marks, off from 1.6970/80 at the open. Dollar/yen was at 113.72/77 compared to 113.60/70.
